title: Match Point (2005) Review - by an Amateur Critic

commenti.body: It’s certainly one of Woody’s best later (post 2000) movies along with Blue Jasmine and Midnight in Paris. It’s fascinating to see a master of his work, a comedy legend, finally really nail the deadly serious film he’d been wanting to get right since his first attempt (Interiors) in 1978. As you say, the film flips convention on its head really impressively with the lead continuing on with his life seemingly unaffected and the parallel to luck in tennis is really interesting. I’m pretty sure Scar Jo was about 19 when this was made which really makes her performance all the more impressive

It's less of a surprise if you've seen Crimes and Misdemeanors, which tells a similar story with older characters.

In both movies, the tragedy is not just the meaningless killing of an innocent woman, but also that the man responsible gets away with it *and* gets over his initial feelings of guilt.  It's dark stuff.
